subject: InfraHealth — performance alignment: end-to-end latency envelopes & streaming constraints
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@infrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: InfraHealth — performance alignment: end-to-end latency envelopes & streaming constraints

Thanks for the productive call earlier today — quick internal + external recap so we're aligned and can move to a concrete benchmark window. I captured the core asks and open questions below. Emma — please correct anything I missed.

Top-level goals (from InfraHealth):
- Improve user-facing E2E latency vs current provider across typical sessions.
- Preserve or improve streaming UX (first-token latency + tail) for long responses.
- Validate p95/p99 under realistic concurrency and burst patterns.

Customer-provided targets / constraints discussed on call:
- Target E2E p95 <= 350 ms, p99 <= 1.1 s (user-facing, includes network).
- Current provider measured roughly p95 ~ 420 ms, p99 ~ 1.5 s for production traffic (per Emma).
- Sustained QPS: ~160 requests/sec. Peak bursts: up to ~420 req/s (10s windows).
- Concurrent live sessions: ~250 simultaneous sessions at peak.
- Typical request size: 120 input tokens; typical response size: 280 tokens.
- Streaming behavior: require first-token p95 <= 120 ms; streaming tail p99 <= 900 ms, with chunk frequency ~150 tokens.

Open questions / data we need from InfraHealth before we run benchmarks:
1) Traffic profile CSV (per-session distribution + burst windows) — Emma said you would upload v2.
2) A small set of representative session traces / sample payloads (including real-world prompts).
3) Clarify whether user-facing E2E measurements should include client-side network hops (they confirmed yes on call).

Proposed Redwood plan (high level):
- Baseline: reproduce current-provider numbers using provided traffic_profile (sanity check).
- Redwood hosted run: equivalent traffic, same model variant where possible, measure p50/p95/p99 and first-token streaming latencies.
- Streaming validation: run chunked responses with identical chunk size/frequency to production sessions.
- Acceptance: p95/p99 targets measured over 30-minute rolling windows; agreement on measurement instrumentation (X-Request-ID, token-timing headers).

Next steps (owners):
- InfraHealth: upload infra_traffic_profile_v2.csv + sample traces (Emma).
- Redwood: prepare test harness and benchmark YAML (Ben/Jonas).
- Decide on two 2-hour test windows next week and nominate test participants (Sofia to coordinate).

Attachments: I will attach a draft benchmark YAML and our streaming spec for clarity (see attachments list).

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
From: Emma Li <emma.li@infrahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: InfraHealth Platform <platform@infrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InfraHealth — performance alignment: end-to-end latency envelopes & streaming constraints

Thanks Sofia — this is great, and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and notes from our side: 

- Confirmed: our observed numbers with the incumbent are nearer p95 ~420 ms and p99 ~1.5 s for the 95/99 windows we've been tracking. We need visible improvement at p95 and at least parity at p99 for short-to-medium sessions.
- Concurrency: our internal telemetry shows ~300 concurrent sessions during the weekday evening ramp (we quoted 250 as a conservative typical peak; please include 300 as a higher test bound).
- Payloads: we'll upload infra_traffic_profile_v2.csv and a tarball of anonymized session traces (7 MB). The traffic profile includes per-session token distributions, time-of-day ramps, and a short sample for burst events.
- Security: we'll share an S3 URL with the traces (read-only) and would like a short NDA clause appended to any signed benchmark report — standard for our procurement.

We'll get the artifacts to you by EOD and can confirm test windows in a follow-up. For measurement: we want the final benchmark report to include the raw timing histograms + token-level timing for a sample 15-minute window.

—Emma
Emma Li
Product Lead, Platform Services
InfraHealth
emma.li@infrahealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@infrahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InfraHealth — performance alignment: end-to-end latency envelopes & streaming constraints

+1 on Sofia's summary. Below is a concrete benchmark playbook I propose (technical):

Benchmark playbook (detailed):
1) Instrumentation & definitions (pre-run)
   - Agree on E2E timing headers (X-Request-ID, X-Client-Timing).
   - Define p95/p99 as percentiles over 30-minute rolling windows; report both raw and aggregated histograms.

2) Baseline reproduction
   - Use InfraHealth's infra_traffic_profile_v2.csv to generate a load test against the incumbent endpoint (we'll run alpha for parity).
   - Capture full token-level timing for a 30-minute sample window.

3) Redwood hosted run (three passes)
   - Pass A: steady-state (sustained 160 rps for 30 min).
   - Pass B: burst profile (repeat 10s bursts up to 420 rps, reproduce session mix).
   - Pass C: streaming/long responses — validate first-token and chunked streaming with chunk size ~150 tokens.
   - For each pass collect p50/p95/p99, first-token latency, token throughput, error rates, and tail distributions per request class.

4) Acceptance criteria (proposed)
   - E2E p95 <= 350 ms and p99 <= 1.1 s for short sessions (<= 300 output tokens) over the 30-minute windows.
   - Streaming: first-token p95 <= 120 ms; streaming tail p99 <= 900 ms.
   - No systemic increase in error rate vs baseline (error delta < 0.5%).

5) Reporting
   - Deliver: raw histograms, per-request sample traces, CSV of token-level timings, and a one-page executive summary mapping to InfraHealth's SLOs.

Logistics / scheduling
- Proposed windows (all times PT): Tue 2027-06-22 10:00–12:00 or Wed 2027-06-23 14:00–16:00. We should pick two slots to run baseline + hosted.
- Owners: Ben (test harness + measurement), Jonas (infra/run coordination), Sofia (scheduling + stakeholder comms).

Security note: we'll only pull traces from the read-only S3 URL Emma provided and redact any PII. We'll include the short NDA clause in the benchmark report if InfraHealth confirms.

Ben
Ben Carter
Staff SE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: InfraHealth — performance alignment: end-to-end latency envelopes & streaming constraints

Thanks Emma — appreciate the quick turnaround. Two quick items to close out: 

1) I've attached our benchmark request YAML (redwood-benchmark-request.yaml) and a short streaming-demo-specs.pdf that mirrors the chunking/frequency settings we discussed. Ben/Jonas will stand up the harness once the traffic artifacts are uploaded.
2) Please confirm test windows: Tue 2027-06-22 10:00–12:00 PT and Wed 2027-06-23 14:00–16:00 PT (we'll do baseline in the first hour and hosted in the second hour of each window). If those work, we'll lock them and send calendar invites.

One more ask for the acceptance report: please confirm whether InfraHealth wants a signed appendix with the NDA clause around benchmark artifacts. If yes, we'll prepare a short templated paragraph.

If there are no objections, we plan to run the first scheduled window next Tue and deliver an initial draft report within 48 hours of the run.

Best — Sofia
